mechanism_narrative: A four-week decline in TRANSIT from -25.1 to -27.6 signals reduced commuting and discretionary trips; this suppresses retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -25.1 to -27.6 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days while TRANSIT remains below -25.0.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM falls below -2.0 (it reached -2.9 at t-0w), households are cutting shopping frequency; this demand weakness spreads to retail, driving RETAIL_REC down over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week after GROCERY_PHARM falls below -2.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of TRANSIT below -25 and WORKPLACES below -10 indicates both transit and office activity are severely suppressed; their interaction reduces weekday retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases when both TRANSIT < -25 and WORKPLACES < -10.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, RESIDENTIAL remaining above 13.5 shows stay-at-home behavior is binding; this curbs retail and recreation outings, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises while RESIDENTIAL remains above 13.5.

mechanism_narrative: A week-over-week PARKS improvement of more than 1.5 points (as from -20.9 to -19.1) signals easing outdoor avoidance; this behavioral shift spills into retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -20.9 to -19.1 from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is lower than or equal to last 28-day mean after PARKS improves by more than 1.5 points week-over-week.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of RESIDENTIAL above 13 and PARKS below -15 means people are staying home and avoiding outdoor activity; the combined mobility suppression lowers retail visits, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises when RESIDENTIAL > 13 and PARKS < -15.

mechanism_narrative: A seasonal late-winter/early-spring rise in PARKS above -20 (it reached -19.1 at t-0w) typically precedes a weather-driven increase in retail and recreation trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying above -20.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES staying below -9.5 for four consecutive weeks indicates a persistent remote-work policy; reduced office footfall weakens nearby retail demand, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES between -9.6 and -10.3 across four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises while WORKPLACES stays below -9.5.
